title: The Knowledge Layer Model (KLM): Evidence-Visible AI Output, Routing Diagnostics, and Negative Results
abstract: arXiv:2610.42066v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: AI answers require more than apparent correctness: reviewers need to inspect their recorded basis. We introduce the Knowledge Layer Model (KLM), an open, implementation-neutral specification for inference records with versioned epistemic assessments, evidence relations, and explicit unknowns. SEDIM, the knowledge and evidence architecture of Nage AI OS, is a reference implementation. We reference KLM v0.3 (repository tag v0.3.0). Empirical material consists of separate internal experiments, not end-to-end validation. A historical platform-domain routing benchmark reports 137/150 classifications across 15 classes (91.3%; nominal 95% Wilson interval 85.7-94.9%); the numerator is recovered from a rounded summary, and historical example membership is unverified. A native-model weight-path configuration yielded 0/15 successful answers in a corrected two-source test. A capacity-growth comparison could not establish a reliable effect because

tldr: 该论文提出知识层模型（KLM），一个开放的、与实现无关的AI推理记录规范，通过带版本管理的认知评估、证据关系和明确的未知项使AI输出可被审查，并如实报告了包含负面结果在内的初步路由诊断实验。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces the Knowledge Layer Model (KLM), an open, implementation-neutral specification for AI inference records that makes outputs reviewable through versioned epistemic assessments, evidence relations, and explicit unknowns, accompanied by preliminary routing diagnostics that honestly include negative results.
